label.description: What this candidate is, in a few words (its topology and hypothesis).

graph.description: A graph of the library to instantiate on the twin (its id, from library.graphs), instead of a spec: its template is resolved with the settings given, the variables you do not name are taken at the graph's defaults (a known constant is held and cannot be fitted; a bounded variable is searched within its bounds), and its own probes are compared with their columns unless compare says otherwise.

settings.description: The settings of the library graph (who is on board: labOccupants, habOccupants); its defaults when absent.

add.description: With graph: nodes and connections added to the library graph once instantiated (a generated source of gas wired into it: its output into an atmosphere's next delta_CO2_<k> input, for instance; a node whose output is a concentration is read where it is, never wired into a volume). The graph's own nodes keep their ids. A connection is {from: [node, port], to: [node, port]}.

persons.description: Who is on board, one entry per person (their module and activity; id, callsign and name when the medical monitor names them): replaces the library graph's roster, the settings follow. The task's observations may list them (observations.persons).

params.description: node parameters; each value is a number, or {"$expr": "formula over the variables"}, or {"$series": {"column": "telemetry column", "scale": "formula", "offset": "formula"}} for the segments of a Logic.Time:timeline driven by a measured column, or {"$first": "telemetry column"}, or {"$initialMasses": {"species": "CO2", "fraction": ..., "unit": "ppm", "volume": "V", "temperatureK": "Tk"}} for a Physics.Scene:atmosphere's _initialMassKg

spec.description: The candidate graph: nodes of the catalogue and their connections [node, port]. Not with graph.

compare.description: Which probe of the graph (node, property) is judged against which telemetry column. A library graph brings its own when absent.

variables.description: Variables held fixed for this evaluation. For a library graph, only names of its interface (the shelf's variables); a graph carries its known constants itself, so this is rarely needed.

fit.description: The bounds of each variable nobody knows: the harness searches them with an optimiser (a few dozen runs). A constant the documentation gives goes in variables, not here.

estimator.description: How the bounds are searched: nelder-mead (default; a simplex search, about 10 to 20 runs per parameter, local) or grid (every combination of evenly spaced levels; levels ^ parameters runs; shows the shape of the cost).

levels.description: For the grid: levels per parameter (5 when absent).

maxRuns.description: Sandbox runs the estimator may spend on this candidate (40 when absent, 80 at most).
